Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National | Top Story 21-year-old Ghanaian Thomas Oduro stabbed to death in North London Source : myjoyonline.com 14 November 2026 8:19pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
A 21-year-old Ghanaian identified as Thomas Oduro has died after being stabbed in north London, prompting a murder investigation by the Metropolitan Police.
The incident occurred on Friday, November 13, along Lordship Lane in Haringey, where emergency services were called shortly after 6 pm following reports that a man had been attacked.
According to the BBC, paramedics attended the scene but were unable to save the victim, who was pronounced dead at the scene.
The Metropolitan Police subsequently identified him as Thomas Oduro, from Tottenham, and confirmed that his next of kin had been informed.
Detective Chief Inspector Phil Clarke, who is leading the investigation, expressed condolences to the bereaved family, saying they had suffered a devastating loss and were receiving support from specialist officers.
He added that investigations were continuing at the scene, with an increased police presence expected in the area over the coming days.
The detective also appealed to anyone who was around Lordship Recreation Ground at about 6 pm on Friday, or who might have information relevant to the incident, to assist investigators.
The police have urged witnesses to contact them through 101 or provide information anonymously to Crimestoppers.
The London killing comes amid growing concern among Ghanaians following several recent deaths involving young nationals in North America.
In the United States, 15-year-old Ghanaian Javits Frimpong was fatally shot on October 29 while walking to school in the Bronx, New York. A 17-year-old suspect was arrested and charged with murder and other offences in connection with the incident.
Another Ghanaian, 24-year-old Joseph Owusu, was found dead at a dumpsite in the Bronx after reportedly going missing for about two weeks. Surveillance footage later emerged showing two individuals removing a large bag believed to contain his body from a car and leaving it on a pavement. His family has called for justice as investigations continue.
In Canada, 18-year-old Ghanaian Prince Abdul Malik was shot dead in Toronto on November 7. Toronto Police identified the victim as Malik Abass, of Mississauga, while his family identified him as Prince Abdul Malik. The killing has been classified as a homicide, with investigations ongoing.
The circumstances surrounding the death of Thomas Oduro in London are still being investigated.
